problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+2x{y}^{′}-12y=2{x}^{2}+1,\,x>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A{x}^{3}+\frac{B}{{x}^{4}}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.

feedback.problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
4{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+2x{y}^{′}-6y=2x-3,\,x>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(x)=\frac{A}{x}+Bx\sqrt{x}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.
feedback.worked_solution:
The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is  $2x-3.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is of the form 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha x+\beta ,
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are the constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=\alpha ,\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=0.
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation and group the terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}\cdot 0+2x(\alpha )-6(\alpha x+\beta ) & =2x-3 \\ (2\alpha -6\alpha )x-6\beta  & =2x-3 \\ -4\alpha x-6\beta  & =2x-3\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-4\alpha =2\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,x) \\ -6\beta =-3\, & (\text{equating the constants})\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{1}{2},\,\,\beta =\frac{1}{2}.$

Hence, the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{x}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.
$$
